recipes.title: Line Trace By Channel
recipes.summary: Cast a line from the camera and read what it hits.

steps.title: Get the camera view
steps.body: From a Player Controller, add Get Player View Point. Use its Out Location as the trace Start, and keep Out Rotation for the next step.

steps.title: Choose the end point
steps.body: Add Get Forward Vector and plug in the camera rotation. Set End to Start + (Forward Vector × distance), for example 5000 units.

steps.title: Add Line Trace By Channel
steps.body: Plug in Start and End. Set Trace Channel to Visibility. Turn Ignore Self on so the trace does not hit the player.

steps.title: Draw it while testing
steps.body: Set Draw Debug Type to For Duration so you can see the line in the level. Turn this back to None when you are done debugging.

steps.title: Branch on the hit
steps.body: Add a Branch and use the Return Value as the Condition. True means something blocked the line.

steps.title: Read the hit
steps.body: Off the True pin, add Break Hit Result. Use Hit Actor, Impact Point, and Impact Normal for the rest of your gameplay.

recipes.title: Open a door on overlap
recipes.summary: When the player enters a box, a Timeline swings the door open.

steps.title: Add a trigger
steps.body: In the door Blueprint, add a Box Collision and size it to the area the player should walk into.

steps.title: Listen for overlap
steps.body: Select the box. In Details, add the event On Component Begin Overlap.

steps.title: Make sure it is the player
steps.body: Off Other Actor, add Cast To your player character class, for example Cast To BP_ThirdPersonCharacter. Other actors are ignored.

steps.title: Add a Timeline
steps.body: Right-click the graph and choose Add Timeline. Open it, add a Float Track from 0 to 1, and set the length, for example 1.0 second.

steps.title: Lerp the rotation
steps.body: From the Cast success pin, call Play on the Timeline. Off Update, add Lerp (Rotator). A is the closed rotation, B is the open rotation (often 0, 90, 0), and Alpha is the Timeline float.

steps.title: Rotate the mesh
steps.body: Add Set Relative Rotation on the door mesh and plug in the Lerp result. Put the mesh pivot on the hinge, or the door will swing from its center.

steps.title: Optional: close it
steps.body: Add On Component End Overlap, Cast To the player again, and call Reverse on the Timeline so the door closes.

recipes.title: Bind an Enhanced Input action
recipes.summary: Create an Input Action, add it to a Mapping Context, and respond in the Event Graph.
nodes: Get Enhanced Input Local Player Subsystem

steps.title: Create an Input Action
steps.body: In the Content Browser, right-click, then Input, then Input Action. Name it, for example IA_Interact. Set Value Type to Digital (Bool) for a button, or Axis1D (Float) for an axis.

steps.title: Create a Mapping Context
steps.body: Right-click, Input, Input Mapping Context. Open it, add a mapping for your Input Action, and bind a key, gamepad button, or mouse button.

steps.title: Expose the context
steps.body: On your Character or Player Controller, add a variable of type Input Mapping Context and assign your IMC asset in Details.

steps.title: Only set up the local player
steps.body: In Event BeginPlay, or Event Receive Controller Changed, add a Branch with Is Locally Controlled so only the owning client adds the context.

steps.title: Add Mapping Context
steps.body: Get Controller, Cast To Player Controller, then Get Enhanced Input Local Player Subsystem. From the subsystem, add Add Mapping Context. Plug in your IMC and a Priority (0 is fine for one context).

steps.title: Add the action event
steps.body: In the Event Graph, right-click and add the event for your Input Action, named after the asset, for example IA_Interact.

steps.title: Pick the right pin
steps.body: Use Started or Triggered for a one-shot button. Use Ongoing plus Action Value for an axis. Build your gameplay off that pin.

recipes.title: Animate with a Timeline
recipes.summary: Use a Timeline float as Alpha to lerp location or rotation over time.

steps.title: Add a Timeline
steps.body: In the Event Graph, right-click and choose Add Timeline. Give it a name, for example TL_Open.

steps.title: Add a float track
steps.body: Double-click the Timeline. Add a Float Track. Add a key at time 0 with value 0, and a key at the end, for example 1.0s, with value 1. Set the length to match.

steps.title: Play or reverse it
steps.body: Use the Play, Play from Start, or Reverse exec pins to start or reverse the animation.

steps.title: Lerp with the update
steps.body: The Update pin fires every frame while it runs and outputs the track value. Use that as Alpha in Lerp, Lerp (Rotator), or VLerp.

steps.title: Apply the result
steps.body: Plug the Lerp result into Set Actor Location, Set Actor Rotation, or Set Relative Rotation, depending on what you are moving.

steps.title: React when it finishes
steps.body: The Finished pin fires when the Timeline reaches the end, or the start if you reversed it. Use it for a sound, a collision change, or a completed state.

recipes.title: Spawn Actor from Class
recipes.summary: Spawn a Blueprint at a transform and keep a valid reference to it.

steps.title: Add Spawn Actor from Class
steps.body: Set the Class pin to the Blueprint you want to spawn, or pass a Class variable.

steps.title: Make a transform
steps.body: Add Make Transform. Location can come from Get Actor Location, a socket, or a Hit Result Impact Point. Set rotation and scale as needed.

steps.title: Handle collisions
steps.body: Set Collision Handling Override. Try To Adjust Location, But Always Spawn is a safe default. Use Do Not Spawn if Colliding if you would rather fail than overlap.

steps.title: Set Owner and Instigator
steps.body: Optionally set Owner and Instigator, often the player pawn or the Player Controller, so damage and ownership stay correct.

steps.title: Check the return value
steps.body: The Return Value is the new actor. Add Is Valid and only use the reference if it spawned.

steps.title: Initialize it
steps.body: To set variables before BeginPlay, expose them on spawn in the actor Blueprint, or call a setup function on the Return Value immediately.

recipes.title: Cast To the player character
recipes.summary: Turn a generic actor into your player class, or fail safely.

steps.title: Start with a generic reference
steps.body: Get an Actor or Pawn first, for example Other Actor from an overlap, Hit Actor from a trace, or Get Player Character.

steps.title: Add Cast To
steps.body: Add Cast To and pick your player Blueprint, for example Cast To BP_ThirdPersonCharacter.

steps.title: Use the success pin
steps.body: The top exec pin is the success path. On that pin the output is a typed reference, so class-specific functions and variables appear.

steps.title: Handle Cast Failed
steps.body: The Cast Failed pin fires when the object is a different class or is not valid. Use it to ignore the event or try another path.

steps.title: Do not recast every tick
steps.body: Store the successful reference in a variable. Later, use Is Valid instead of casting again.

steps.title: Prefer interfaces when needed
steps.body: If many actor types should respond, use a Blueprint Interface instead of a chain of Cast To nodes.

recipes.title: Call a Blueprint Interface
recipes.summary: Send a message to any actor that implements your interface, with no Cast To chain.

steps.title: Create the interface
steps.body: In the Content Browser, right-click, Blueprints, Blueprint Interface. Name it, for example BPI_Interact. Open it and add a function, such as Interact, with any inputs you need.

steps.title: Implement it on the target
steps.body: Open the actor that should react, such as a door, pickup, or NPC. In Class Settings, add the interface under Implemented Interfaces.

steps.title: Build the event
steps.body: In that actor's Event Graph, Event Interact, or your function name, now appears. Build the reaction there.

steps.title: Get the target on the caller
steps.body: On the player or the object that starts the interaction, get the target actor, for example Hit Actor from a line trace.

steps.title: Optional: check first
steps.body: Add Does Implement Interface, set Interface to BPI_Interact, then a Branch, so you only message valid targets.

steps.title: Send the message
steps.body: From the target, add the message node Interact (Message). It shows an envelope icon. You do not need Cast To.

recipes.title: Set Timer by Event
recipes.summary: Run work on a repeating timer instead of Event Tick.
nodes: Clear and Invalidate Timer by Handle

steps.title: Prefer a timer to Tick
steps.body: Use a timer when the work only needs to run every so often, for example every 0.2 seconds, instead of Event Tick.

steps.title: Add a Custom Event
steps.body: Add a Custom Event for the repeating work, for example Fire Pulse or Refresh Trace.

steps.title: Start the timer
steps.body: At the start, on BeginPlay or when the ability starts, add Set Timer by Event. Drag from the Event pin and select your Custom Event.

steps.title: Set time and looping
steps.body: Set Time to the period in seconds. Set Looping to true if it should repeat.

steps.title: Store the handle
steps.body: Promote the Return Value to a variable of type Timer Handle so you can stop it later.

steps.title: Clear it when done
steps.body: When the ability ends, add Clear and Invalidate Timer by Handle and pass that handle. This is cheaper and safer than leaving Event Tick running.

recipes.title: Create a widget and add it to the viewport
recipes.summary: Spawn a Widget Blueprint, show it, then remove it and restore game input.

steps.title: Make the widget
steps.body: Create a Widget Blueprint, for example WBP_InteractPrompt, and design the UI there.

steps.title: Create Widget
steps.body: In the player or Player Controller graph, add Create Widget. Set Class to your widget, and set Owning Player to Get Player Controller.

steps.title: Keep a reference
steps.body: Promote the Return Value to a variable so you can update or remove the same widget later.

steps.title: Add to Viewport
steps.body: Off the Create Widget exec pin, add Add to Viewport and plug in the widget reference.

steps.title: Switch input if needed
steps.body: If the widget needs a cursor, Get Player Controller, Set Show Mouse Cursor to true, and Set Input Mode UI Only, or Game and UI if the game should still receive input.

steps.title: Close it cleanly
steps.body: Call Remove from Parent on the widget, then Set Input Mode Game Only and hide the cursor. Use Is Valid before removing if it might already be gone.

recipes.title: Get Player Controller and Enable Input
recipes.summary: Find the local player controller, enable input on an actor, or possess a pawn.

steps.title: Get Player Controller
steps.body: Add Get Player Controller. Player Index 0 is the local player in a single-player game.

steps.title: Read the pawn or view
steps.body: From the controller you can Get Controlled Pawn, Get Player View Point, or Set Show Mouse Cursor.

steps.title: Enable Input on an actor
steps.body: To let a usable object receive input, add Enable Input on that actor and pass the Player Controller.

steps.title: Disable it later
steps.body: Pair it with Disable Input when the interaction ends so keys stop firing on that actor.

steps.title: Get a look direction
steps.body: For aim or placement, Get Control Rotation from the Player Controller, then Get Forward Vector if you need a world direction.

steps.title: Possess a new pawn
steps.body: After spawning or swapping pawns, use Possess on the Player Controller with the new pawn. Use UnPossess if you need to drop control first.

recipes.title: Launch Character
recipes.summary: Kick a Character with a world-space velocity, or use Add Impulse on a physics mesh.

steps.title: You need a Character
steps.body: Launch Character only works on a Character, or a child of Character, not a raw Pawn or Actor. Get a Character reference, or Cast To Character.

steps.title: Add Launch Character
steps.body: Launch Velocity is a world-space vector, for example (0, 0, 800) for an upward hop, or Get Actor Forward Vector × speed plus some Z.

steps.title: Set the override flags
steps.body: XY Override, if true, replaces the current horizontal velocity. Z Override, if true, replaces the vertical velocity. Turn Z Override on for a consistent jump or bounce.

steps.title: Call it once
steps.body: Call it from an overlap, an input event, or a hit. Calling it every tick will fight movement and feels wrong.

steps.title: Physics meshes use Add Impulse
steps.body: For a simulating Static Mesh or Skeletal Mesh, use Add Impulse on the primitive component. Turn on Vel Change if you want a mass-independent kick.

recipes.title: Get All Actors Of Class and For Each Loop
recipes.summary: Find every actor of a class and run work on each one, but not on Tick.

steps.title: Get All Actors Of Class
steps.body: Add Get All Actors Of Class and set Actor Class to the type you want, such as your pickup class, enemy class, or a parent class.

steps.title: Add For Each Loop
steps.body: The Out Actors pin is an array. Add For Each Loop and plug the array in.

steps.title: Use the loop body
steps.body: Loop Body runs once per actor. Array Element is the current actor. Array Index is its position in the array.

steps.title: Filter inside the loop
steps.body: Put the per-actor work on Loop Body. Use a Branch inside the loop if only some actors should be affected.

steps.title: Use the Completed pin
steps.body: The Completed pin fires after the last element. Use it for a summary, a Delay, or the next step in a Sequence.

steps.title: Do not run this on Tick
steps.body: Get All Actors Of Class is expensive. Run it on BeginPlay, a timer, or a one-shot event, not Event Tick.

recipes.title: Is Valid and Branch
recipes.summary: Guard destroyed references and split logic on a boolean.

steps.title: References can go stale
steps.body: When you store an actor, component, or widget in a variable, it can become stale if the object is destroyed.

steps.title: Use the Is Valid exec node
steps.body: Add the exec node Is Valid, which has Is Valid and Is Not Valid pins, and plug in the object before you read it or call a function on it.

steps.title: Exit on the failure pin
steps.body: Put the real work on the Is Valid pin. On Is Not Valid, clear the variable or exit early so you do not get an Accessed None warning.

steps.title: Use Branch for booleans
steps.body: For a plain boolean check, use Branch. Give it a Condition, then build the True and False paths.

steps.title: There is also a pure Is Valid
steps.body: A pure Is Valid node returns a boolean you can plug into Branch. Use whichever reads more clearly in the graph.

steps.title: Common conditions
steps.body: Typical conditions are Return Value from a trace, Does Implement Interface, or Equal (Object) to compare with the player.

recipes.title: Delay and Sequence
recipes.summary: Fire several actions in order, and wait on one path without pausing the game.

steps.title: Add a Sequence
steps.body: Add a Sequence node when several actions should start in a fixed order from one event, such as Event BeginPlay.

steps.title: Pins fire in order
steps.body: Then 0, Then 1, and Then 2 fire in order in the same frame, unless a Delay or another latent node pauses a path.

steps.title: Add a Delay
steps.body: Add Delay on a path that should wait. Set Duration in seconds. Execution continues on the completed pin after the wait.

steps.title: Delay is latent
steps.body: Delay only works on an execution path in an Actor or Component Blueprint, not in a pure function.

steps.title: It does not pause the game
steps.body: A Delay does not pause the whole game, only that execution path. Other events still run.

steps.title: Use a timer if it must cancel
steps.body: For work that must be canceled, such as an ability wind-up the player can interrupt, use Set Timer by Event and Clear and Invalidate Timer by Handle instead of Delay.

recipes.title: Play Sound at Location
recipes.summary: Play a one-shot sound in the world, or attach a looping sound to an actor.

steps.title: Get a sound asset
steps.body: Import a Sound Wave, or create a Sound Cue if you need variation, attenuation, or concurrent limits.

steps.title: Play Sound at Location
steps.body: Add Play Sound at Location. Set Sound to your asset. Set Location to the source, for example Get Actor Location or a Hit Result Impact Point.

steps.title: Volume and pitch
steps.body: Adjust Volume Multiplier and Pitch Multiplier if needed. Leave them at 1.0 unless you want a change.

steps.title: Follow a moving actor
steps.body: For a sound that should follow an actor, such as footsteps or a machine, use Spawn Sound Attached and attach it to a mesh or scene component.

steps.title: Stop a looping sound
steps.body: Promote the Return Value of Spawn Sound Attached to an Audio Component variable, then call Stop or Destroy Component.

steps.title: Add 3D falloff
steps.body: Assign an Attenuation Settings asset, or configure attenuation on the Sound Cue, so the sound gets quieter with distance.
